raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates prominent central pulmonary arteries (particularly the right descending pulmonary artery), which is a classic radiological sign of pulmonary hypertension resulting from chronic thromboembolic disease. There is no evidence of pleural effusion, cardiomegaly, or diffuse infiltrates to support the other options.
